I'm double-checking the 4.00 dimension against alternate reference points, but none of the outer face or centerline measurements land cleanly on 4.00. Now I'm testing the 5.86 segment the same way, comparing it against the centerline distance to see if that matches better.

Interestingly, 121.89→287.93 gives almost exactly 5.86, suggesting the label might be using the wall centerline rather than the face-to-face convention used elsewhere in the chain. But that would be inconsistent with the adjacent 11.5 segment, which clearly uses wall faces, and mixing conventions would break the total sum to 10.00. It looks like 5.86 is actually 5.80 plus half a wall thickness (0.0575), which is a suspicious coincidence — the label may be mismatched with the actual drawn segment length of 5.80.

Checking the chain sums with different combinations of 5.80/5.86 and 4.00/3.485 against the 0.30 and 0.115 offsets, neither alternate pairing sums to 10.00 — only the original actual values do. So both labels appear to be wrong, and I'll flag this using the chain-sum failure as the key diagnostic, then move on to double-checking the room areas, since 31.2 m² doesn't cleanly match any natural width/height combination I can derive from the dimensions.

I try testing whether the labeled ratios (31.2:13.4:6.9) match the actual computed ratios (37.12:14.24:7.67), but they don't align cleanly. I also try backing out alternative room dimensions that might reconcile the discrepancy, but none of the combinations produce consistent numbers either.

Checking the label positions against the room layout, WOHNEN, SCHLAFEN, and BAD all seem correctly matched to their respective rooms, so the mismatch isn't a labeling error—it's a genuine inconsistency between the stated areas and the drawn geometry across all three rooms.

I should stick to reporting what's actually drawn versus what the labels claim, rather than trying to reverse-engineer some "intended" correct version of the plan. Testing whether a cleaner set of dimensions (like 10.00×7.00 overall with standard wall thicknesses) could explain the discrepancies, but the numbers don't reconcile consistently across all rooms, so I'll just document the measured vs. labeled differences directly.

I'm also checking whether the labeled room areas match what the labeled dimensions would actually produce — they don't, confirming these are genuine errors rather than rounding. Beyond the five numeric mismatches, I'm noting that the bathroom being accessible only through the bedroom is a real circulation flaw worth flagging, even though it could be read as an intentional ensuite layout.

content.text:
Looking at the door swings, I notice the bathroom is only accessible through the bedroom — there's no direct access from the living area, which seems worth flagging as a layout issue. I'm also checking the short "11.5" dimension segment where the label placement looks off.

I also notice none of the rooms have window openings, but since this looks like a schematic test plan, I'll treat that as a simplification rather than a hard error. I'll focus my findings on the measurable dimension and area discrepancies, plus the bathroom-access layout note, structuring each as a finding with labeled and comparison values where numeric data applies.

I'm debating whether to report the dimension-chain mismatch (10.575 vs 10.00) as its own finding or fold it into the two segment-label errors, since it's really a consequence of those. I'll keep it separate since it's a distinct, checkable inconsistency that's useful to flag, clearly explaining it stems from the segment errors. Now I'm tallying up everything I've verified: three room labels, three area labels, six dimension labels, the vertical 7.00 measurement, and the scale.

I'm counting the remaining items to check — scale notation, plan number, date, project text, door swings, and wall thicknesses — bringing the total to about 24, then moving on to write the final answer since there's nothing worth saving to memory for this one-off task.

I've measured everything against the drawn vector geometry (scale 1:100 confirmed — the 10.00 and 7.00 overall dimensions both check out exactly).

**Errors found:**

| Element | Plan says | Measured |
|---|---|---|
| Dim segment, left room width | 5.86 | 5.80 m |
| Dim segment, right rooms width | 4.00 | 3.485 m |
| Dim chain sum vs overall | 10.00 | chain sums to 10.575 m |
| WOHNEN area | 31.2 m² | 5.80 × 6.40 = 37.12 m² |
| SCHLAFEN area | 13.4 m² | 3.485 × 4.085 = 14.24 m² |
| BAD area | 6.9 m² | 3.485 × 2.20 = 7.67 m² |

Correct: overall 10.00 × 7.00, both 30 cm outer walls, the 11.5 cm partition, all three door openings (1.00 / 1.00 / 0.90 m) with matching swing radii, title block scale.

Also worth the author's attention: the only bathroom (BAD) opens solely off SCHLAFEN, so it can only be reached by walking through the bedroom.

findings.explanation: The dimension line segment carrying the label '5.86' measures 164.41 pt = 5.800 m at 1:100. The label is 6 cm too large. (5.86 would be the distance to the partition CENTRELINE, but the neighbouring segment is dimensioned as the full 11.5 cm wall thickness, so the chain uses wall faces; mixing conventions double-counts half the wall.)

findings.element: Lower dimension chain, segment between right face of the partition (x=289.56 pt) and inner face of right exterior wall (x=388.35 pt) — width of SCHLAFEN/BAD
findings.explanation: The segment labelled '4.00' actually measures 98.79 pt = 3.485 m at 1:100 — 51.5 cm shorter than labelled. This is the largest single discrepancy on the sheet and would be a real problem if the contractor sets out the partition from this figure.

findings.kind: dimension chain does not sum to the overall dimension
findings.element: Lower dimension chain (30 + 5.86 + 11.5 + 4.00 + 30) versus the overall dimension 10.00 above it
findings.explanation: Adding the printed sub-dimensions gives 0.30 + 5.86 + 0.115 + 4.00 + 0.30 = 10.575 m, but the overall dimension directly above says 10.00 m and the building is in fact drawn 283.46 pt = 10.000 m wide. The chain is internally impossible: no set of walls can satisfy both. Consequence of the two wrong segment labels above; with the drawn values (0.30 + 5.80 + 0.115 + 3.485 + 0.30) the chain closes at exactly 10.00.
The clear internal size of WOHNEN as drawn is 5.800 m x 6.400 m = 37.12 m2. The stated 31.2 m2 is 5.9 m2 (16%) too small — it looks like a transposition/typo of 37.12.

Clear internal size as drawn is 3.485 m x 4.085 m = 14.24 m2 (measured from the inner face of the top exterior wall, y=433.70 pt, to the top face of the 11.5 cm partition, y=549.50 pt). The stated 13.4 m2 is 0.84 m2 too small. Note it is also not the area you would get from the labelled 4.00 m width (that would be 16.34 m2), so the area does not agree with either the drawing or the dimension labels.

Clear internal size as drawn is 3.485 m x 2.200 m = 7.67 m2 (from the underside of the 11.5 cm partition, y=552.76 pt, to the inner face of the bottom exterior wall, y=615.12 pt). The stated 6.9 m2 is 0.77 m2 too small. The three labelled areas total 51.5 m2 against 59.0 m2 of actual net floor area.

findings.element: Door between SCHLAFEN and BAD (0.90 m opening in the horizontal partition at y=549.50-552.76 pt), and absence of any door from WOHNEN to BAD
findings.explanation: BAD has exactly one door and it opens into SCHLAFEN. The apartment's only bathroom can therefore be reached only by passing through the bedroom; the entrance door leads into WOHNEN, WOHNEN connects only to SCHLAFEN, and SCHLAFEN connects to BAD. Flagging in case an ensuite was not intended — if it was, ignore. (The door geometry itself is fine: all three swing radii equal their opening widths.)

findings.explanation: Adding the printed sub-dimensions gives 0.30 + 5.86 + 0.115 + 4.00 + 0.30 = 10.575 m, but the overall dimension directly above says 10.00 m and the building is in fact drawn 283.46 pt = 10.000 m wide. The chain is internally impossible: no set of walls can satisfy both. Consequence of the two wrong segment labels above; with the drawn values (0.30 + 5.80 + 0.115 + 3.485 + 0.30) the chain closes at exactly 10.00.
The clear internal size of WOHNEN as drawn is 5.800 m x 6.400 m = 37.12 m2. The stated 31.2 m2 is 5.9 m2 (16%) too small — it looks like a transposition/typo of 37.12.

Clear internal size as drawn is 3.485 m x 4.085 m = 14.24 m2 (measured from the inner face of the top exterior wall, y=433.70 pt, to the top face of the 11.5 cm partition, y=549.50 pt). The stated 13.4 m2 is 0.84 m2 too small. Note it is also not the area you would get from the labelled 4.00 m width (that would be 16.34 m2), so the area does not agree with either the drawing or the dimension labels.

Clear internal size as drawn is 3.485 m x 2.200 m = 7.67 m2 (from the underside of the 11.5 cm partition, y=552.76 pt, to the inner face of the bottom exterior wall, y=615.12 pt). The stated 6.9 m2 is 0.77 m2 too small. The three labelled areas total 51.5 m2 against 59.0 m2 of actual net floor area.

findings.element: Door between SCHLAFEN and BAD (0.90 m opening in the horizontal partition at y=549.50-552.76 pt), and absence of any door from WOHNEN to BAD
findings.explanation: BAD has exactly one door and it opens into SCHLAFEN. The apartment's only bathroom can therefore be reached only by passing through the bedroom; the entrance door leads into WOHNEN, WOHNEN connects only to SCHLAFEN, and SCHLAFEN connects to BAD. Flagging in case an ensuite was not intended — if it was, ignore. (The door geometry itself is fine: all three swing radii equal their opening widths.)

structured_output.summary: Six measurable errors: two dimension labels in the lower chain contradict the drawn geometry (5.86 should be 5.80, and 4.00 should be 3.485), which is why the chain adds up to 10.575 m against the 10.00 m overall dimension, and all three room area annotations are too small (WOHNEN 31.2 vs 37.12 m2, SCHLAFEN 13.4 vs 14.24 m2, BAD 6.9 vs 7.67 m2). The overall 10.00 x 7.00 envelope, both 30 cm exterior walls, the 11.5 cm partition, the three door openings and their swing radii, and the stated 1:100 scale all check out exactly. Separately, worth confirming the layout is intended: the only bathroom is reachable solely through the bedroom.
